caption: Figure 1. Overview of TSGR, a unified generative framework that jointly handles retrieval and pre-ranking within a single model. (a) Parallel SID Construction builds a three-level codebook using category and cluster priors at Levels 1–2, and query-aware codebooks at Level 3. (b) Generative Backbone performs hierarchical beam search with prefix-constrained decoding at Levels 1–2 and standard beam search at Level 3. VRM re-ranks candidates by fusing SID embeddings with item side-info.
Figure 2. Training Pipeline. Model capabilities are developed progressively via Pre-SFT multi-task pretraining and SFT with a weighted multi-positive loss.

Figure 3. Comparison of different QP-SID configurations and training strategies. HR@1000 and HR@100 are reported for each combination of input/label configuration (rows) and efficiency ID strategy (columns).
Figure 4. Ablation study on the effect of different score combinations in the VRM.
Figure 5. Ablation study on the effect of different architecture variants in the VRM.

Figure 6. Ablation study on Pre-SFT task design. Each variant adds a single task on top of the Encoding base, while
Multi-task Fusion trains all tasks jointly.
Figure 7. Online deployment architecture of TSGR. Items generated by TSGR bypass pre-ranking and enter the ranking stage directly.

Figure 8. Case study of QP-SID on two clusters: phone cases (Cluster (140, 3504)) and dining tables (Cluster (10278, 7631)). For each cluster, we show the default value ordering (red) and the query-conditioned ordering under a specific term (blue), with matched terms highlighted in red. Scores beside each item denote the corresponding value scores.

Figure 9. Case study of term selection in QP-SID during serving. Left : different queries each match a single term, which determines the corresponding Level-3 SID. Right : when a query matches multiple terms, QP-SID selects the top-ranked term (solid arrow) and discards the others (dashed arrows). Matched terms are highlighted in red.
